source_user: Choose between tensor and pipeline parallelism for a latency-sensitive multi-GPU service. State the assumptions needed. Scenario variant 290: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. corrected_answer: For scenario variant 290, the supplied facts do not justify a universal TP or PP choice; select conditionally from measured candidates. Assume the model graph, parameter and activation shapes, precision, GPU count, usable HBM in GiB, topology, measured link bandwidth/latency, software and clock state, request-length/arrival distributions, concurrency, batching policy, and latency, throughput, error, quality, and availability SLOs are specified. Separate measured values from estimates and record uncertainty. Enumerate topology-compatible TP degrees and PP stage partitions. Reject any candidate with non-positive HBM headroom after weights, activations, KV/cache and runtime reserve, invalid placement, unsafe collective/activation routes, or no tested rollback path. TP shards computation and can reduce per-rank memory, but synchronized collectives can sit on the critical path; PP can reduce collectives but incurs activation transfers, stage imbalance, pipeline bubbles, and queueing. For interactive latency use the real request mix and the smallest feasible microbatch (often one request); do not import training batch assumptions. Falsifiable hypothesis: under the stated fixed workload and hardware, the feasible candidate with the lower measured p99 end-to-end latency will also meet the latency SLO without increasing error rate or reducing throughput/availability below their gates; pre-register the threshold and an uncertainty rule before looking at results. Run randomized, interleaved A/B trials for each candidate with warm-up, identical model outputs/quality checks, fixed software and power state, and disjoint tuning and evaluation windows. Hold request traces, seeds where applicable, concurrency, batch limits, timeouts, and autoscaling policy constant; report p50/p95/p99 latency in ms, throughput in requests/s, HBM in GiB, collective/transfer time, queueing, stage utilization, error rate, and confidence intervals. Repeat across representative prompt lengths and load levels, and control for cache state, placement, thermal throttling, background traffic, retries, and drift. Treat a result as provisional if confidence intervals overlap the decision threshold or if any SLO/quality gate fails. In an authorized isolated test, inject a worker/link or stage failure and measure detection, in-flight request behavior, recovery time, availability, and reconfiguration correctness; never perform this on production traffic. Roll back to the last known-good configuration on SLO breach, error/quality regression, unsafe HBM margin, or recovery failure, with a versioned configuration and health check. Choose TP only when its measured collective cost and failure behavior win; choose PP only when transfers, balance, bubbles, and queueing remain acceptable. Otherwise retain the safer known-good configuration and collect the missing evidence.

Run randomized, interleaved A/B trials for each candidate with warm-up, identical model outputs/quality checks, fixed software and power state, and disjoint tuning and evaluation windows. Hold request traces, seeds where applicable, concurrency, batch limits, timeouts, and autoscaling policy constant; report p50/p95/p99 latency in ms, throughput in requests/s, HBM in GiB, collective/transfer time, queueing, stage utilization, error rate, and confidence intervals. Repeat across representative prompt lengths and load levels, and control for cache state, placement, thermal throttling, background traffic, retries, and drift. Treat a result as provisional if confidence intervals overlap the decision threshold or if any SLO/quality gate fails. In an authorized isolated test, inject a worker/link or stage failure and measure detection, in-flight request behavior, recovery time, availability, and reconfiguration correctness; never perform this on production traffic. Roll back to the last known-good configuration on SLO breach, error/quality regression, unsafe HBM margin, or recovery failure, with a versioned configuration and health check. Choose TP only when its measured collective cost and failure behavior win; choose PP only when transfers, balance, bubbles, and queueing remain acceptable. Otherwise retain the safer known-good configuration and collect the missing evidence.
risks: No platform measurements or SLO values are supplied, so a universal TP/PP recommendation would be unjustified.
Tail latency can be confounded by batching, queueing, topology, stage imbalance, cache state, or environmental drift.
Failure injection and reconfiguration can affect availability if not isolated and authorized.
evidence_required: Measured HBM headroom, topology, collective and activation-transfer costs, and feasible stage partitions for every candidate.
Randomized paired trials with disjoint tuning/held-out evaluation across representative lengths and loads, including p99 uncertainty and SLO gates.
Authorized isolated failure/recovery and rollback validation with measured detection, recovery, availability, and correctness.
